faq.q: What is the origin of Shadia?
faq.a: Shadia is associated with Arabic. Shadia is Arabic شَادِيَة (Shādiya), the feminine of شَادِي, meaning 'singer'.
Yes — the underlying form شَادِيَة is Arabic.
Shadia can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Shadia should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Shādiya is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Shadia, shadia. Script forms are شاديه, شادیه, شادیہ, شَادِيَة, शादिया.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
